title: The Saturday move that became Monday
context: A customer phones a moving company after his booking is changed.
script: Hi Claire, it’s Naveen Pillai. I booked a move for this Saturday, but I just got an email saying it’s been changed to Monday. I can’t do Monday. My lease at the old place ends Sunday night.

Let me pull that up. Pillai, Burnaby to Coquitlam, two-bedroom. Yes, I see it. I’m so sorry about that. One of our trucks broke down this week, and our dispatcher moved some Saturday jobs to Monday. Nobody was supposed to do that without phoning you first.
Well, somebody did. I’ve taken Saturday off work, and I’ve got friends coming to help carry the heavy stuff.
I understand. The morning is completely full, but I do have a two o’clock slot.
Two o’clock is late, honestly. The elevator booking at my new building ends at five. If we start at two, we’ll be loading until four, and then there’s a twenty-five minute drive. I won’t make it.
Okay, that’s a fair point. Can you hold for a minute? Let me check with the dispatcher.

Thanks for waiting. Good news. A customer cancelled, so I can give you twelve-thirty with the full crew of three. And because of the mix-up, I’ll take fifteen percent off. Your original quote was six hundred and forty dollars.
Twelve-thirty works. That’s a decent discount, too. Thank you.
You’re welcome. One thing, though. My crew won’t disconnect plumbing, so if you’re taking the washing machine, please have it unhooked and drained the night before.
Right, I’ll do that on Friday evening. Will I get a confirmation?
You’ll have an email within the hour, and this time it will say Saturday.

questions.q: Why is Naveen calling?
o: He wants to cancel his move
He needs a larger truck for his furniture
His moving date was changed without his agreement
He was charged more than his quote
questions.e: He says he booked Saturday but received an email moving the job to Monday, which he cannot do.

questions.q: What caused the change to Naveen’s booking?
o: A truck broke down
The crew was short of workers
Naveen asked for a later date
The weather forecast was bad
questions.e: Claire says one of the trucks broke down and the dispatcher pushed Saturday jobs to Monday.

questions.q: How much will Naveen pay after the discount?
questions.e: Fifteen percent of 640 is 96, and 640 minus 96 is 544.

questions.q: Why does Naveen refuse the two o’clock slot?
o: He has to be at work in the afternoon
He would not finish loading in time to use the elevator booking
His friends are only free in the morning
He wants to avoid the highway traffic
questions.e: The elevator booking ends at five, loading would run until four, and the drive takes twenty-five minutes.

questions.q: What time will the movers arrive on Saturday?
o: Morning, before noon
questions.e: Claire offers twelve-thirty with a full crew of three after the cancellation.

questions.q: What does Claire expect Naveen to do before Saturday?
o: Pay a deposit online
Label every box by room
Reserve the elevator again
Disconnect and drain the washing machine
questions.e: She says the crew will not disconnect plumbing, so the washer must be unhooked and drained the night before.

title: No lesson on Tuesday
context: A mother calls a community centre because her daughter’s swimming class has been cancelled.
script: Hi Greg, this is Imani Okafor. I got a text this morning saying my daughter’s Level 3 swim class on Tuesdays is cancelled. Can you tell me what’s going on?
Oh, yes, I’m sorry. The instructor took a full-time job at another pool and left last week. We’re still looking for a replacement, so we’ve had to cancel the Tuesday class for now.
So what are my options? I paid ninety-six dollars for the session.
Let me look. We have a Thursday class at five-fifteen with two spots left.
Thursday’s tricky. I work until five-thirty, and the drive here takes me about twenty minutes. She’d always be late.
Right. Then there’s Saturday at nine, but that one’s full. There’s a waiting list with three families on it, so I wouldn’t count on it.
Wednesday at six-fifteen. There’s one space. The catch is that class already had its first lesson, so she’d start one week behind.
That’s not a big deal, as long as she can catch up. Is the instructor good with beginners? She’s a bit nervous in the deep end.
Marcus is great with kids who are nervous. He’s been teaching here for six years. And to make up for the missed lesson, I can give her a free drop-in swim pass for a weekend.
Oh, that’s kind. Then let’s do Wednesday at six-fifteen.
Done. The fee stays the same, so you don’t pay anything extra. If you’d rather have a refund, that takes ten business days, but you’d lose the spot.
No, no, Wednesday is fine. Thanks for sorting it out so quickly.
My pleasure. You’ll get a confirmation email this afternoon.

questions.q: Why does Imani phone the community centre?
o: She wants to ask about a refund policy
Her daughter’s regular class has been cancelled
She is registering her daughter for the first time
Her daughter was hurt in the pool
questions.e: She received a text saying the Tuesday Level 3 class was cancelled and asks what is going on.

questions.q: Why was the Tuesday class cancelled?
o: Too few children signed up
The pool is being repaired
The instructor is sick
The instructor accepted a job elsewhere
questions.e: Greg says the instructor took a full-time job at another pool and left.

questions.q: Why can’t Imani use the Thursday class?
o: She finishes work too late to get there on time
The class is already full
Her daughter has another lesson on Thursdays
The class is for a higher level
questions.e: Class is at five-fifteen, Imani works until five-thirty and needs twenty minutes to drive.

questions.q: What does Greg suggest about the Saturday class?
o: She should put her name down and expect a spot soon
It is the best choice for beginners
It is unlikely that she will get in
It is cheaper than the other classes
questions.e: It is full with three families waiting, and he says “I wouldn’t count on it.”

questions.q: Why does Greg offer a free drop-in swim pass?
o: To encourage her to bring friends
To compensate for a lesson her daughter will miss
To thank her for being patient with the centre
To replace the refund she is not receiving
questions.e: He offers it “to make up for the missed lesson” because Wednesday’s class has already started.

questions.q: What will Imani do?
o: Wait for a Tuesday instructor to be hired
Ask for a refund in ten business days
Enrol her daughter in the Wednesday evening class
Take the Thursday class and arrive late
questions.e: She says “let’s do Wednesday at six-fifteen” and turns down the refund.

title: The connection that keeps dropping
context: A small-business owner calls his internet provider about repeated outages.
script: Northlink Internet support, you’re speaking with Fiona.

Hi, Tomasz Wozniak here. My internet has been cutting out every evening between seven and nine for two weeks. A technician came on Tuesday, swapped my modem, and it dropped again last night. Frankly, I’m running out of patience.
I’m sorry, that’s frustrating. Let me look at your line history. Hmm, I can see the drops, and the signal readings show a lot of noise on the line outside your house, not inside it.
So the modem he replaced wasn’t the problem?

Not the main one. Your old modem was about three years old and was throwing errors too, so the swap wasn’t a waste, but it wasn’t the root cause. I’d say the technician fixed a minor fault and missed the major one.
There’s a fault ticket open for your whole street. A repair crew is scheduled for Thursday, between eight and noon, but they’ll be working at the junction box, so you don’t need to be home.
I do bookkeeping for small businesses, and I have a tax filing deadline Friday. Evening outages are exactly when I do my uploads.
Understood. In the meantime, I can lend you a mobile hotspot at no charge. It comes with fifty gigabytes of data, and a courier can have it to you tomorrow before noon.
That helps. What about compensation? I’m paying eighty dollars a month for something that doesn’t work.
I can apply a twenty-five dollar credit right now. Anything beyond that has to be approved by a supervisor, so I’ll submit a request and note your business use. I can’t promise the outcome.
Fair enough, at least you’re honest about it. I’ll take the hotspot and the credit, and we’ll see what the supervisor says.
Thank you for your patience, Mr. Wozniak. You’ll get a text with the courier tracking number within the hour.

questions.q: What is the main reason Tomasz is calling?
o: An earlier repair did not stop recurring outages
He wants to cancel his service
He received a bill he does not understand
He needs help installing a new modem
questions.e: Internet drops every evening for two weeks, and the modem swap did not fix it.

questions.q: According to Fiona, what is causing the outages?
o: A faulty modem inside his home
Too many devices on his network
Interference on the line outside his home
A planned upgrade by the company
questions.e: She says the readings show noise on the line outside his house, not inside it.

questions.q: What does Fiona suggest about the technician’s visit?
o: It was unnecessary
It dealt with a smaller problem but not the main one
It caused the current outages
It solved the problem temporarily
questions.e: She says the old modem was throwing errors too, so the swap wasn’t a waste, but it wasn’t the root cause.

questions.q: What will Tomasz receive by tomorrow before noon?
o: A $25 credit on his bill
A visit from a repair crew
A replacement modem
A mobile hotspot with 50 gigabytes of data
questions.e: Fiona offers a free hotspot with fifty gigabytes that a courier can deliver before noon tomorrow.

questions.q: How does Tomasz feel at the end of the call?
o: Completely satisfied with the outcome
Convinced the company is being dishonest
Determined to switch providers
Still unhappy but willing to cooperate
questions.e: He appreciates her honesty and accepts the hotspot and credit while waiting on the supervisor, though he began frustrated.

questions.q: Why does Fiona say she “can’t promise the outcome”?
o: The repair date might change
A larger credit needs a supervisor’s approval
The courier may be late
Business customers are not eligible for credits
questions.e: She can apply twenty-five dollars herself, but anything more must be approved by a supervisor.

title: A missed connection in Toronto
context: A traveller speaks to an airline agent after arriving late for a connecting flight.
script: Next in line, please. Hi there, how can I help?
Hi. I’m Zainab Rahimi. My flight from Winnipeg landed forty minutes late and I missed my connection to Halifax. I have a job interview at ten-thirty tomorrow morning downtown.
I’m sorry to hear that. Let me see what we can do. The delay was caused by a storm over Manitoba, so it’s weather-related. That affects what we can cover, but I’ll go through your options.

Option one is tonight’s flight through Montreal, leaving at nine-forty and landing in Halifax at ten past midnight. I can confirm your seat. Option two is a direct flight tomorrow at six-thirty that gets in at nine.
Nine is cutting it close. By the time I get my bag and take a taxi into the city, it’s nearly ten. If anything slips, I’m not there.
That’s a risk, yes. But there’s one thing about tonight’s route. With the tight connection in Montreal, your checked bag might not make the transfer, and it could arrive on the morning flight.
Honestly, I can live with that. My interview outfit is in my carry-on. The suitcase is mostly clothes for the week.
In that case, I’d suggest tonight, too. If your suitcase does arrive late, we’ll deliver it to your hotel at no charge. Just give me the address.
It’s the Harbour View on Barrington Street. Will the airline pay for the hotel tonight, since I’ll be arriving after midnight?

I wish I could say yes. Because the delay was due to weather, which is outside our control, hotels aren’t covered. What I can do is give you a fifteen dollar meal voucher for the wait this evening. I know it’s not much.
It’ll cover a sandwich. Thank you for being straightforward, Owen.
Of course. Here’s your boarding pass. Gate twenty-two, and boarding starts at nine-ten.

questions.q: What is Zainab’s problem?
o: She missed a connecting flight because of a late arrival
Her luggage was lost in Winnipeg
She was given the wrong boarding pass
Her flight to Halifax was cancelled
questions.e: Her flight landed forty minutes late and she missed the connection to Halifax.

questions.q: What risk does Owen mention about tonight’s flight?
o: Her suitcase might not arrive at the same time as she does
The flight might be overbooked
Her seat could be given away
The plane might leave late
questions.e: He says the checked bag might miss the tight transfer in Montreal and come on the morning flight.

questions.q: Why does Zainab prefer tonight’s flight?
o: It lands earlier in the city
It is a direct flight
The morning flight leaves too little time before her interview
It includes a hotel voucher
questions.e: Landing at nine would mean nearly ten by the time she gets to the city, which is too close to ten-thirty.

questions.q: Why does Owen mention the storm?
o: To warn her that tonight’s flight may be delayed
To apologise for the airline’s mistake
To explain why the airline will not pay for her hotel
To persuade her to take the morning flight
questions.e: He says weather is outside their control, so hotels are not covered.

questions.q: How would you describe Owen’s manner?
o: Impatient and dismissive
Sympathetic but firm about company policy
Casual and unconcerned
Uncertain about the rules
questions.e: He says “I wish I could say yes” and apologises, yet does not offer the hotel.

questions.q: What will happen if Zainab’s suitcase arrives late?
o: She must collect it at the airport
The airline will refund the baggage fee
It will be sent to her home address
It will be delivered to her hotel free of charge
questions.e: Owen says they will deliver it to her hotel at no charge.

type: Listening to a Daily Life Conversation
title: Thanksgiving for the stranded
context: Two friends plan a Thanksgiving dinner for people who cannot travel home.
script: So, are we really doing this? Thanksgiving dinner for everybody who can’t go home?
I think so. I counted last night. Dev, Priyanka, Mei, Tyler, Ana and her cousin who just moved here, plus the two of us.
That’s eight. Okay. Where are we cooking? My oven is tiny.
Mine, definitely. I’ll host it at five on Sunday. My dining table only seats six, though, so we’ll borrow two chairs from my neighbour.
Good plan. What about the turkey? A whole one is too much for eight people.
Yeah, the smallest one at the store is twelve pounds. I was thinking turkey breast instead. It cooks faster, too.
Done, I’ll order it from the butcher on Fifth Avenue. But Dev’s vegetarian.
He said he’ll bring a lentil loaf, and honestly, it’s better than most turkeys. Priyanka can’t eat gluten, so she’s bringing the mashed potatoes and a gravy made with cornstarch.
Mei’s making an apple crisp, and I’ll buy a pumpkin pie. I tried baking one last year and the crust was like cardboard.
Ha, I remember. Then I’ll bring drinks and take care of the cleanup afterwards. I’m better at washing dishes than cooking anyway.
You’re a lifesaver. Oh, and can you make a playlist? Nothing too loud, just background music.

questions.q: What are Jasmine and Luis mainly discussing?
o: Where to spend the holiday weekend
How to cook a turkey
A trip to see their families
Plans for a holiday dinner with friends
questions.e: They are arranging a Thanksgiving dinner for people who can’t go home.

questions.q: How many people will be at dinner?
o: Eight
Six
Seven
Ten
questions.e: Six friends plus Jasmine and Luis make eight, and Luis confirms “That’s eight.”

questions.q: Why will they cook a turkey breast rather than a whole turkey?
o: The butcher has no whole turkeys
A whole bird would be too big for the group
Luis’s oven is too small
Dev prefers it
questions.e: Luis says a whole turkey is too much for eight, and the smallest is twelve pounds.

questions.q: What can be inferred about Jasmine’s baking?
o: She enjoys baking desserts for friends
She is allergic to wheat
She does not trust herself to make a good pie
She has never used her oven
questions.e: She says she’ll buy a pie because last year’s crust was like cardboard.

questions.q: What will Luis be responsible for?
o: Drinks, dishes and music
The main course and dessert
Chairs and decorations
Mashed potatoes and gravy
questions.e: He offers to bring drinks and do the cleanup, and he will make a playlist.

type: Listening to a Daily Life Conversation
title: What do you buy for Grandma?
context: A brother and sister talk about a gift for their grandmother’s eightieth birthday.
script: Okay, so Grandma’s birthday is in three weeks. Have you thought about what to get her?
Kind of. I was thinking a tablet, so she can video-call us. She keeps complaining that she never sees the kids.
Hmm. I’m not sure. She still has trouble with her phone. Last time I called, she accidentally hung up twice.
True. But the new ones have really big buttons. Mom said they cost around two hundred and fifty dollars.
That’s a lot if she never uses it. What about something personal? I found those old slides from Grandpa’s trip to Newfoundland in the garage. I could have them turned into a digital photo album.
Oh, I love that. She’d cry. How much would that cost?
A shop on Queen Street does it for about a dollar fifty a slide. There are around eighty slides. So that’s one hundred and twenty dollars.
Okay, that’s cheaper than the tablet. And honestly, a bit more thoughtful.
Right, but she can’t really use a USB stick either. We’d need a digital picture frame to show them.
There you go, so we could get the frame as well. It’s about eighty dollars. Together that’s two hundred, still under the tablet.
Perfect, and we split it. One hundred each.
Not yet. She can’t keep a secret. She’d tell Grandma by Friday.
You’re not wrong. Let’s keep it between us until the party.

questions.q: What are Mei and Carlos trying to decide?
o: Where to hold a party
What to give their grandmother
Who should call their grandmother
How to organize old photographs
questions.e: They are discussing birthday gift ideas for their grandmother.

questions.q: Why is Carlos unsure about the tablet?
o: It is too expensive for a gift
She already owns one
Their grandmother struggles with technology
Mom disagrees with the idea
questions.e: He says she has trouble with her phone and hung up twice, and he worries she won’t use it.

questions.q: How much will the slide-scanning cost?
questions.e: About eighty slides at a dollar fifty each is one hundred and twenty dollars.

questions.q: Why do they decide to buy a digital frame?
o: Their grandmother cannot use a USB stick
The frame is cheaper than a tablet
The slides are too fragile to display
She asked for one
questions.e: Carlos says she can’t use a USB stick, so they need a frame to show the photos.

questions.q: Why do they keep the plan from their mother?
o: She would object to the cost
She has already bought something similar
They think she would give away the surprise
She wants to pay for it herself
questions.e: Carlos says she can’t keep a secret and would tell Grandma by Friday.

type: Listening to a Daily Life Conversation
title: The open-concept experiment
context: Two coworkers talk during a break about their office’s new open layout.
script: So, week two of the open-concept experiment. How are you holding up?
Let’s say I’ve learned more about Raj’s lunch than I ever wanted to. Yesterday it was curry, and the whole floor knew by eleven.

Ha. To be fair, I’ve noticed fewer emails and more people just walking over to ask questions. Yesterday I solved a problem with accounting in two minutes. Normally that would’ve been three days of back and forth.
That part I’ll give them. The collaboration is real. But I can’t concentrate. I’ve started coming in at seven-thirty, just to get quiet time before everyone arrives.
Wow, that’s early. I thought management said they’d set up quiet rooms.
They did, four of them, for sixty people. By nine-thirty they’re all booked, and people are using them for phone calls, not for focused work.
So maybe the real problem isn’t the layout, it’s the number of rooms.
Maybe. Though I’m not convinced more rooms would fix it. If you need a room for half the day, what was the point of removing the walls?
Okay, that’s fair. Though the company did save money. They gave up the second floor, didn’t they?
Yes, which is exactly why I suspect this was never about collaboration. It’s about rent.
You might be right. But I’m trying to keep an open mind. Management said they’ll review it in three months, and they’re sending a survey next week.
A survey. Great. I’ll fill it out honestly, though I doubt it changes anything.
Well, the least we can do is say clearly what isn’t working. Maybe suggest headphone zones and a no-calls area?
Now that’s a good idea. Send me that in writing, and I’ll back you up.

questions.q: What is Gordon’s main complaint about the new office?
o: It is difficult to concentrate
Meetings take too long
Lunch is not allowed at desks
There are too many emails
questions.e: He says he can’t concentrate and arrives early for quiet time.

questions.q: Which benefit of the new layout does Beth mention?
o: She enjoys the noise of the office
She sits next to her friends
The office looks more modern
She can resolve questions faster in person
questions.e: She solved a problem with accounting in two minutes that would have taken three days by email.

questions.q: Why does Gordon say the quiet rooms are not helping?
o: They are too small to work in
They are used up early, and often for calls
Few employees know about them
They are on a different floor
questions.e: He says they are booked by nine-thirty and used for phone calls rather than focused work.

questions.q: What does Gordon suspect about the company’s motive?
o: It wanted to monitor employees
It expected productivity to rise
Saving on rent was the real reason for the change
It planned to hire more staff
questions.e: He says the company gave up the second floor and “it’s about rent.”

questions.q: What is Beth’s attitude toward the change?
o: Strongly opposed
Cautiously open-minded
Completely enthusiastic
Indifferent
questions.e: She says she is trying to keep an open mind and suggests constructive improvements.

type: Listening to a Daily Life Conversation
title: A dog in a rental?
context: Two friends discuss whether one of them should adopt a dog.
script: Okay, tell me honestly. Am I being ridiculous? I’ve been looking at the shelter’s website every night this week.
Not ridiculous. Though you did say in March that you’d never have time for a pet.
I know, I know. But since I started working from home three days a week, the apartment feels so quiet. There’s a beagle called Biscuit who looks like she needs a home.
Biscuit. Of course. Well, what does your landlord say? I thought your lease said no pets.
It said no dogs over twenty-five pounds. Biscuit’s twenty-two. I checked twice.
Fine, that’s clever. But what about the other two days, when you’re in the office? Beagles don’t love being left alone for nine hours.
That’s my worry. There’s a dog walker in my building who charges forty dollars a visit. If I use her both office days, that’s eighty dollars a week, which I didn’t even think about until you asked.
Plus food, vet bills, a deposit. It adds up. I’m not trying to talk you out of it, but my sister adopted a puppy last year and she says the first two months were a lot harder than she expected.
Biscuit isn’t a puppy. She’s four, already house-trained, and the shelter says she’s calm.
That does change things. Have you thought about fostering first? Some shelters let you try it for a couple of weeks.
Actually, I hadn’t. That’s a smart idea. If it doesn’t work, nobody gets hurt, least of all the dog.
Exactly. I’d do that before signing anything.
You’re right. I’ll ask about it tomorrow. Honestly, I think I just needed someone to say the sensible thing out loud.
Happy to be the sensible one. You can buy me coffee for it.

questions.q: What is Olivia’s main reason for wanting a dog?
o: She wants to exercise more
Her family is encouraging her
She is in a pet-friendly building
She feels lonely at home since working remotely
questions.e: She says the apartment feels quiet since she started working from home three days a week.

questions.q: Why does Olivia believe she can have Biscuit in her apartment?
o: The landlord gave verbal permission
The lease does not mention pets
The lease only bans dogs over 25 pounds
She will keep the dog at a friend’s place
questions.e: She says the lease prohibits dogs over twenty-five pounds, and Biscuit weighs twenty-two.

questions.q: How much would the dog walker cost each week?
questions.e: Forty dollars a visit on both office days comes to eighty dollars a week.

questions.q: Why does Kwame mention his sister’s experience?
o: To recommend a particular breed
To talk Olivia out of adopting at all
To suggest Olivia ask her for advice
To caution Olivia that early months can be harder than expected
questions.e: His sister found the first two months much harder than expected, and he says he is not trying to talk Olivia out of it.

questions.q: What does Olivia decide to do?
o: Ask the shelter about fostering Biscuit first
Adopt Biscuit immediately
Hire a dog walker for five days a week
Wait until she finds a larger apartment
questions.e: She calls fostering “a smart idea” and says she will ask about it tomorrow.

title: A message from the dental office
context: A receptionist leaves a voicemail about a changed appointment.
script: Hello, this message is for Mr. Ellis. It’s Harpreet calling from Brightsmile Dental on Maple Street. I’m calling because Dr. Chen has been called away to a training course on Thursday, so we have to move your cleaning appointment. It was booked for Thursday the sixth at nine-thirty in the morning.
The earliest new time we have is Friday the seventh at two-fifteen in the afternoon. The cleaning takes about forty-five minutes, and our office closes at five on Fridays, so there’s plenty of time.

Please arrive ten minutes early, because we’ll need to update your forms. And don’t forget to bring your insurance card. Your plan covers the cleaning, but we do need to see the card. If you’ve changed jobs or insurance since your last visit, please tell us when you arrive.

If Friday doesn’t work for you, no problem. Just call us back at six-oh-four, five-five-five, oh-one-four-eight, and we’ll find another day. We’re open Monday to Friday, eight to five. Please let us know by noon on Wednesday, because after that we’ll hold the Friday time for you and it will count as a missed appointment. There’s a fifty dollar fee for missed appointments with less than a day’s notice.
We’re sorry for the inconvenience. Thanks very much, Mr. Ellis, and have a good day.

questions.q: Why is Harpreet calling Mr. Ellis?
o: To confirm a booking he made yesterday
To ask him to pay a bill
To reschedule his appointment
To tell him about a new dentist
questions.e: She says the dentist is away, so the Thursday cleaning has to be moved.

questions.q: When is Mr. Ellis’s new appointment?
o: Thursday at 9:30 a.m.
Friday at 2:15 p.m.
Friday at 9:30 a.m.
Monday at 2:15 p.m.
questions.e: She gives Friday the seventh at two-fifteen in the afternoon.

questions.q: What time should Mr. Ellis arrive at the office?
questions.e: She asks him to arrive ten minutes early, which is 2:05.

questions.q: By when must Mr. Ellis tell the office if the new time does not work?
o: Noon on Wednesday
Five o’clock on Thursday
Noon on Friday
Eight o’clock on Monday
questions.e: She says to let them know by noon on Wednesday.

questions.q: Why was the original appointment cancelled?
o: The office is closing for a holiday
The dentist will be at a training course
The cleaning equipment is broken
Mr. Ellis’s insurance expired
questions.e: Dr. Chen has been called away to a training course on Thursday.

title: All aboard at Millbrook
context: A guide welcomes visitors before a ride on a heritage steam train.
script: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the Millbrook Heritage Railway. I’m Rosa, and I’ll be your guide today. Before we board, let me explain how the day works.

Our locomotive, Number Seventeen, was built in 1912, and she’s still burning coal. The ride covers fourteen kilometres out to Cedar Bridge and back, and the whole trip takes fifty minutes. Trains leave the station every hour, on the hour, starting at ten. The last departure is at four o’clock.

If you haven’t bought tickets yet, adults are twenty-two dollars, and children from four to eleven are twelve dollars. Children under four ride free. We also have a family pack for four people, up to two adults and two children, for sixty dollars. Tickets are sold at the window beside the gift shop, and we take cards, but cash is welcome too.

A few safety notes. Please stay seated while the train is moving, and keep your arms and heads inside the windows. The steam engine produces sparks and smoke, so we’ve asked everyone to keep windows closed in the tunnel, which is about two minutes in.

At Cedar Bridge, we stop for five minutes. That’s the best place to take photos, and you’re welcome to step out onto the platform. Please don’t wander past the yellow line, and listen for the whistle when it’s time to get back on.

After the ride, the museum in the station building is open until five. Admission is free for ticket holders, and there’s a short film every half hour about how the railway was built. Now, if you’ll follow me, we’ll head to platform one. Enjoy the ride.

questions.q: What is the guide mainly doing?
o: Explaining how the visit will work
Selling tickets to visitors
Telling the history of the locomotive in detail
Warning visitors about dangers on the track
questions.e: She says she’ll explain how the day works and covers schedule, prices, safety and the museum.

questions.q: How long does the train ride take?
o: 14 minutes
35 minutes
One hour and ten minutes
50 minutes
questions.e: She says the whole trip takes fifty minutes.

questions.q: How much does a family with two adults and two children aged 7 and 10 save by buying the family pack?
questions.e: Individual tickets would cost 22 + 22 + 12 + 12 = 68 dollars; the pack costs 60, so they save 8.

questions.q: When does the last train leave?
o: Hourly until noon
questions.e: Trains leave on the hour, and the last departure is at four o’clock.

questions.q: Where may passengers get off the train to take photos?

title: Winter term at Harbourview College
context: A college staff member makes an announcement to students about registration and parking.
script: Good afternoon, students. This is Ms. Adeyemi in Student Services with some important updates for the winter term. Please listen carefully, because there’s been a correction.

First, registration. Last week’s email said registration opens for everyone on November fourth. That was a mistake. Registration is staggered. Students who have completed sixty or more credits can register starting November third. Students with thirty to fifty-nine credits can register on November fifth. Everyone else, including first-year students, can register on November seventh. Registration closes on December fifteenth, which is also when tuition is due. If you need a payment plan, apply before December first. There’s a seventy-five dollar late fee after the fifteenth.

Second, parking. Lot C will be closed for construction from November twentieth until the end of January. Permits for lot C remain valid, but they’ll be honoured in lot F, which is behind the sports centre. A shuttle will run between lot F and the main entrance every twelve minutes, from seven in the morning until nine at night. Allow an extra fifteen minutes on your first few days.
Third, the library will stay open until midnight from December fourth to December eighteenth for exam preparation. Normal hours resume on the nineteenth.

Finally, academic advisors hold drop-in hours on Tuesdays and Thursdays from one to four, no appointment needed. If you’re unsure which courses to take, I’d strongly recommend you go before your registration date rather than after, since popular classes fill quickly.
That’s everything for now. Thank you, and good luck with your registration.

title: Riverton’s new collection schedule
context: A recorded information line explains changes to the city’s garbage and recycling service.
script: You’ve reached the City of Riverton Waste Services information line. This message explains changes to household collection that begin Monday, January twelfth.

Under the new schedule, organics, that’s your green bin, will be collected every week instead of every second week. Garbage and recycling will now alternate. If recycling is collected this week, garbage will be collected next week, so each is picked up once every two weeks. The reason for the change is that food scraps make up nearly half of what households throw away, and the city aims to keep seventy percent of waste out of the landfill by the year 2030.

Because garbage pickup will be less frequent, please note the limits. Each household may put out one garbage bin of up to one hundred and twenty litres. Extra bags are accepted only with a three-dollar tag, which you can buy at any library or community centre.

Bulky items such as couches and mattresses are collected on request. Each household receives two free pickups a year, and you must book at least five working days ahead. A third pickup costs twenty-five dollars.

Collectors will check bins. If a bin contains items that don’t belong, such as plastic bags in the green bin, they’ll leave a tag explaining the problem and won’t empty it. You can remove the items and put the bin out again on your next scheduled day.
When a holiday falls between Monday and Friday, collection moves to the next day for the rest of that week, so Friday pickups shift to Saturday.
To look up your schedule, visit the city website or press two now. To speak to a representative, press three. Our staff are available weekdays, eight to four-thirty.
